newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schaeuble rejects politicians role in wage debate.
newsitem.headline: Schaeuble rejects politicians role in wage debate.

text.p: Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) said on Wednesday that he thought politicians had no role to play in the debate over wages and working hours in Germany.
"On the matter of working hours, union and employer wage negotiators are better placed to solve the conflict than politicians," Schaeuble said at the second day of a union-organised jobs conference.
Schaeuble's comments appeared to undermine the chances for a renewed attempt at last year's failed "alliance for jobs" pact between government, unions and employers.
The pact sought to link wage moderation by unions to job creation measures by employers and the government.
Schaeuble was reacting to a suggestion from IG Metall chief Klaus Zwickel that the union favoured in principle the idea of a 32 hour workweek.

Schaeuble said he accepted that unemployment in Germany was currently too high, but was met by calls for concrete solutions to Germany's unemployment problems from the 500-plus participants at the jobs conference.
On the issue of European-wide job creation measures, he said he was a very strong supporter of the concept of subsidiarity rather than seeking centralised solutions to such problems as employment.

He added that he had no doubt that greater harmonisation of tax systems and social standards would come about in Europe, but at the moment there existed "great" discrepancies in European Union countries.
He said as a result, national fiscal policy still had a large role to play in addressing issues such as high regional unemployment.
